Telemetry schema (v0)#

Normative source: web/playground/telemetry.js (client), the POST /v1/telemetry handler in web/playground/serve.mjs (sink), and the call sites in render-worker.js / main.js. Everything below is read from that code as of 2026-09-11.

Design law #5: every session reports. Telemetry is a same-origin POST to /v1/telemetry carrying either a frame-time batch (every 10 s) or a reliability event (as it happens). It must never break the app: every send is wrapped so a failure is swallowed.

No PII#

  • The session id is crypto.randomUUID() generated at boot and held only in memory — no cookie, no localStorage, nothing survives a reload. (the analytics feed additionally keeps a random browser id in localStorage so returning visitors count once — stored server-side only as a keyed hash, never under an opt-out; see the look-and-stall feed.)
  • No user id, no IP is recorded client-side (the server appends the raw body only; it does not add the remote address).
  • What is sent about the device: adapter name, backend, tier, navigator.userAgent, in-app WebView classification. These are device fingerprint fields, not identity fields. Consent gating for partner pages is P3 scope per the source comment (not implemented — not verified beyond that comment).

Two session ids#

There are two independent createTelemetry(session) instances, each with its own UUID:

InstanceWhereSends
Render-worker telemetryrender-worker.js, created on init unless golden modeFrame-time batches
Main-thread telemetry (mainTelemetry)main.js, module scope; exposed as window.__verseTelemetryEventReliability events

Consequences: a batch and an event from the same page tab carry different session values, and a watchdog restart spawns a fresh render worker and therefore a fresh batch session id (the main-thread id persists for the tab's lifetime). Joining the two streams is not possible from the payloads alone.

The embed host (embed-host.js) drives the same render worker, so embedded viewers send batches. It defines no __verseTelemetryEvent, so **no reliability events are sent from embeds** (only the playground main.js emits them).

Frame-time batch#

Sent by maybeFlush(now), which the render loop calls after every rendered frame. A flush happens when both hold: ≥ 10 000 ms since the last flush (FLUSH_MS) and at least one CPU sample was recorded. Histograms and counters reset to zero after each flush, so every batch is a disjoint window. Transport: fetch POST, Content-Type: application/json, keepalive: true.

Code
{
  "v": 0,
  "session": "<uuid>",
  "ts": 1757600000000,
  "adapter": "Apple M2",
  "backend": "WebGPU",
  "tier": "A",
  "hasTimestamps": true,
  "mode": "sab",
  "inApp": null,
  "capTier": "A/B",
  "ua": "Mozilla/5.0 …",
  "frames": 612,
  "cpu": { "hist": [0, 0, …32 ints…], "p50": 0.65, "p95": 1.09 },
  "gpu": { "hist": [ … ], "p50": 1.83, "p95": 4.36 }
}
FieldTypeSourceMeaning
v0constantSchema version.
sessionstringcrypto.randomUUID() in the render workerPer-worker-lifetime id (see above).
tsnumberDate.now() at flushWall-clock ms.
adapterstringengine.adapter_name (wgpu adapter info name)GPU adapter fingerprint. May be empty when the browser hides it.
backendstringengine.backendRendering backend as reported by the wasm engine (exact string values not verified here).
tier"A" | "B" | "C"engine.tier (verse-rhi Tier)Engine tier: A = WebGPU with max_storage_buffer_binding_size > 128 MiB and max_buffer_size > 256 MiB; B = other WebGPU adapters; C = the WebGL2 build.
hasTimestampsbooleanengine.has_timestampsWhether GPU timestamp queries are available; when false gpu is always null.
mode"sab" | "fallback"render workersab = sim worker + SharedArrayBuffer triple buffer; fallback = single-worker camera-only world (page not cross-origin isolated).
inAppstring | nullmsg.caps?.inApp — intended source caps.inApp (caps.js inAppBrowser)WebView classification from the UA: instagram, facebook, whatsapp, pinterest, tiktok, snapchat, line, twitter, or null for a real browser. Currently always null: neither main.js nor embed-host.js puts a caps object on the render worker's init message (they pass only tierC), so the field is wired on the receiving side but never populated.
capTier"A/B" | "C" | "-" | nullmsg.caps?.tier — intended source caps.tier (caps.js detect)Pre-engine capability tier: A/B = WebGPU adapter + OffscreenCanvas, C = WebGL2 only, - = neither (poster + link-out; such a page never boots the engine). Currently always null for the same reason as inApp.
uastringnavigator.userAgentRaw UA string.
framesintCPU sample countFrames rendered in this window (frames with a non-positive CPU time are not counted).
cpu.histint[32]Bucket counts of render-worker CPU time per frame: wall time of engine.render_packed / engine.frame (performance.now() delta) — not the whole rAF callback.
cpu.p50, cpu.p95number | nullPercentiles estimated from the histogram (see below).
gpuobject | nullengine.gpu_frame_msSame shape for the last completed GPU frame time (timestamp queries). null when no GPU sample landed in the window (no timestamps, or gpu_frame_ms is NaN — the WebGL2 backend always reports NaN).

setMeta() replaces the whole meta object; the fields above are the only ones the render worker sets.

Histogram buckets#

32 log-spaced buckets covering 0.25 ms … 64 ms, four buckets per octave:

  • edge(i) = 0.25 · 2^(i/4) ms; bucket i covers [edge(i), edge(i+1)).
  • index(ms) = floor(log2(ms / 0.25) · 4), clamped to [0, 31]. Times below 0.25 ms land in bucket 0; times ≥ ~53.8 ms (edge 31) land in bucket 31, which is therefore open-ended. NaN, 0, and negatives are dropped (not counted in frames).
  • Bucket edges (ms): 0.25, 0.30, 0.35, 0.42, 0.50, 0.59, 0.71, 0.84, 1.0, 1.19, 1.41, 1.68, 2.0, 2.38, 2.83, 3.36, 4.0, 4.76, 5.66, 6.73, 8.0, 9.51, 11.3, 13.5, 16.0, 19.0, 22.6, 26.9, 32.0, 38.1, 45.3, 53.8, (64).
  • Percentile p: the midpoint edge(i + 0.5) of the first bucket at which the cumulative count reaches count · p, rounded to two decimals; 64 if never reached; null when count == 0. So p50/p95 are bucket midpoints, not exact values — the ~19 % bucket width bounds the error.

The same stats() numbers feed the playground HUD (cpuP50, cpuP95, gpuP50, gpuP95).

Reliability events#

telemetry.event(kind, detail) sends immediately, one POST per event, via navigator.sendBeacon (survives page teardown) or fetch POST when sendBeacon is unavailable (no Content-Type header in that path).

Code
{ "session": "<uuid>", "kind": "event", "event": "watchdog-restart",
  "detail": "no heartbeat 8s", "t": 1757600000000 }
FieldMeaning
sessionThe main-thread telemetry UUID (all events go through mainTelemetry).
kindAlways "event" — distinguishes this record from a batch (which has v and no kind).
eventOne of the kinds below.
detailString(detail ?? "") truncated to 300 chars.
tDate.now().
eventEmitted fromdetail
watchdog-restartmain.js watchdog: no message from the render worker for > 8 s while the page is visible and not in XR; the worker is terminated and rebuilt (up to 5 restarts, then "giving up")"no heartbeat 8s"
recoveredmain.js on the render worker's recovered message (GPU device lost and re-created in place)"<ms>ms" — recovery time
uncaughtwindow error listenere.message
unhandled-rejectionwindow unhandledrejection listenerString(e.reason)
engine-errormain.js on a render-worker error message (wasm engine failure)the engine's message
render-worker-errormain.js renderWorker.onerror (worker script failed to parse/start)Called with an object { message }, which String() collapses to "[object Object]" — the message text is lost in the payload as written.

degraded is not a telemetry event. It is an embed-SDK event (verse:event with name: "degraded", detail { tier, inApp, reasons } from embed-host.js when caps land on tier -, or { reason: "iframe-unavailable" } from embed.js when the iframe never reports ready within 8 s). It reaches the partner page's viewer.on( "degraded") listeners and viewer.events(); nothing posts it to /v1/telemetry. Single-thread degraded mode (no SAB) is visible in batches as mode: "fallback", not as an event.

Guided-tour events#

The onboarding tour (web/playground/onboarding.js) sends product events through the same event() call, on every page that has a tour. In the app they share the main-thread session id; on the product page, Studio and the docs the module creates its own in-memory createTelemetry instance, so the id is again a per-page-load UUID. detail is a JSON string holding the surface (landing, app, studio, docs) and a step id — nothing else.

eventWhendetail
tour-startedThe visitor starts or resumes a tour{surface, step, source} — source is chip, nav, url (a ?guide= link) or api (verseOnboarding.start(), e.g. the assistant)
tour-stepA step is reached for the first time (furthest step only, so going back sends nothing){surface, step, n, of}
tour-step-skippedA step's control is not on the page, so the tour moved past it{surface, step}
tour-completedThe last step's button is pressed{surface, steps}
tour-skippedThe tour is closed before the end{surface, step, n, of}
tour-chip-dismissedThe first-visit chip is closed without starting{surface}

Server-side sink#

POST /v1/telemetry in serve.mjs (dev server and production alike):

  • Reads the body up to a hard cap of 1 000 000 characters; a body that would exceed it destroys the connection.
  • Does not parse or validate the JSON. It replaces every newline with a space and appends the body as one line to web/playground/ingest/.telemetry.jsonl (the ingest volume, so it survives redeploys — REL-12), then answers 204.
  • No API key and no rate limit are applied on this route (only /v1/ingest is keyed/rate-limited).
  • Dotfiles are never served: any request whose path has a segment starting with . gets 404, so .telemetry.jsonl, .verse-keys.json and .verse-usage.json cannot be downloaded (audit P0 fix).
  • The source comment says a ClickHouse sink "takes over in P3"; the JSONL file is the only local sink, but the server can batch-forward the same lines to an external collector (below).

Forwarding (INF-5)#

When the environment variable VERSE_TELEMETRY_URL is set, the server forwards telemetry to it in addition to the local JSONL (which keeps being appended exactly as before — it is the fallback and the QA surface):

  • Every accepted POST /v1/telemetry body (newlines flattened, \n terminated — the same line the JSONL gets) is queued in memory.
  • Every 15 s the queue is drained into a POST to VERSE_TELEMETRY_URL with Content-Type: application/x-ndjson, at most 500 KB of lines per batch (always at least one line, so an oversized line cannot wedge the queue). If VERSE_TELEMETRY_AUTH is set, the request carries Authorization: Bearer <value>.
  • A non-2xx response or a network error puts the batch back at the front of the queue (order preserved) for the next tick. The queue is capped at 5 MB; beyond that the oldest lines are dropped, and the drop count is reported in a server log line at most once a minute.
  • Nothing is retried across a restart — the queue is in-memory only. The local JSONL is the durable record.

The ndjson body is ClickHouse-HTTP-compatible: point the URL at https://<clickhouse>/?query=INSERT%20INTO%20telemetry%20FORMAT%20JSONEachRow (ClickHouse accepts ndjson bodies for FORMAT JSONEachRow), or at any collector that accepts newline-delimited JSON. Lines are forwarded unparsed and unvalidated, exactly as received — the collector must treat them as untrusted input, same as JSONL consumers.

Each line of .telemetry.jsonl is therefore either a batch object or an event object, distinguishable by the presence of "v": 0 vs "kind": "event". Because the server appends whatever it receives, consumers should treat lines as untrusted input.

Look-and-stall feed (2.5)#

web/playground/look-feed.js, started by main.js (playground, /view) and embed-host.js (embeds). While a scene is live, one row every 2 s (SAMPLE_MS, the documented sampling rate — not a fraction of sessions: every opted-in session samples at this rate):

Code
{"kind":"look","v":1,"session":"<uuid>","scene":"ingest/<id>.vpk",
 "t":1760000000000,"pos":[3.71,3.13,5.3],"yaw":-125.0,
 "streaming":true,"stalled":false,"walking":false}
  • pos — the camera eye (metres, scene space; 2 decimals); yaw — the view direction in degrees (atan2(forward.z, forward.x)).
  • streaming — bytes were still arriving since the previous sample (the resident-KB counter grew) or the complete-mode loader was up.
  • stalled — streaming while the visitor stood still (moved < 0.5 m) or the loader held the page: waited for the scene here.
  • walking — walk mode was on (playground only; embeds send false).
  • Transport sendBeacon (fallback fetch keepalive); hidden tabs skip samples; a 429 backs off 15 minutes like the batches.

The session id is the page's main-thread telemetry UUID (playground) or a fresh in-memory UUID per embed load. No IP is stored: the sink appends the body only. Opt-outs, decided client-side before the first row: ?analytics=0 (or ?telemetry=0) on the link, the embed option analytics: false (→ ?analytics=0 on the iframe), or a browser sending Do Not Track. Golden mode sends nothing, as before.

The server folds these rows per scene (web/playground/analytics.mjs) into the heatmap grid + funnel GET /v1/scenes/<id>/heatmap returns and Studio draws over the floor plan: opens (a session's first row of any kind on a day), entered (≥ 1 look row), walked (walk mode or ≥ 2 m of path), 30 s and 2 min of look samples. Same window as the per-scene opens: the current log plus one rotation.

4.0: views, actions, browser id, batching#

For the client-facing dashboard (GET /v1/scenes/<id>/analytics, see API) the same module also sends:

Code
{"kind":"view","v":2,"session":"<uuid>","vid":"<uuid>","scene":"ingest/<id>.vpk","t":1760000000000,
 "dev":"phone","os":"ios","app":"instagram","via":"share","ref":"none"}
{"kind":"act","v":1,"session":"<uuid>","vid":"<uuid>","scene":"ingest/<id>.vpk","t":1760000000000,"act":"hotspot","target":"kitchen"}
{"kind":"act","v":1,"session":"<uuid>","vid":"<uuid>","scene":"ingest/<id>.vpk","t":1760000000000,"act":"enquiry"}
  • view — once per scene per page. dev/os/app are computed on the device from fixed lists (deviceOf in look-feed.js); via is embed inside an iframe, share with a ?share= token, else direct.
  • act — interact (first pointer, touch, wheel or key on the page while a scene is live), enquiry (the owner's enquiry button), hotspot (a hotspot opened — target = its id from the experience manifest), link (a hotspot card's link — target = its id), question (a question asked in Ask Verse while the scene is open — the count only, the text is never sent), cta (an interactivity hotspot card's call-to-action — Book a visit, WhatsApp — target = the hotspot id; sent as a beacon) and object (an interactive object used — a door, a switch, Empty room — target = its id; the interactivity hotspots log hotspot / link like the experience ones). target must match [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}, anything else is dropped. (Before the viewer report, hotspot meant the card link.)
  • view.ref (viewer report) — the referring site's class, from a fixed list (referrerOf in look-feed.js): whatsapp, instagram, facebook, linkedin, twitter, youtube, google, search, email, other, or none (no referrer, or this same site). The referrer URL itself never leaves the page — it can carry a search query or a message id.
  • vid — a random UUID kept in localStorage (verse.vid) so a returning browser counts once. Never created under an opt-out; the server stores only a keyed hash of it.
  • Look rows are buffered and posted as {"kind":"batch","rows":[…]} every ~10 s (5 samples), flushed with sendBeacon on visibilitychange → hidden and pagehide. The server stores one line per row.
  • Opt-outs (added): Global Privacy Control, and ?analytics=never, which is remembered on that browser (localStorage verse.analytics=off, the browser id deleted) until ?analytics=1. The server also drops analytics rows sent with DNT: 1 or Sec-GPC: 1.
  • Server side, every view/look/act row is rebuilt from a whitelist (sanitizeRow in analytics-report.mjs) — the stored line is no longer the raw body for these kinds — and they draw from their own rate bucket.

Cadence summary#

SignalWhenTransport

Look (2.5)every 2 s while a scene is live, tab visible, not opted outsendBeacon (fallback fetch keepalive)

Whether batches are sent while the tab is hidden depends on whether the render loop runs (rAF is paused by the browser); not verified.
